subject: Q2 accuracy sprint — stage locks & tidy-up (please action)
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Q2 accuracy sprint — stage locks & tidy-up (please action)

Team —

Quick request as we head into the finance close window. Finance asked for a clean pass on deals that will be considered "commit" for Q2. Please do the following by EOD Thursday: 

- Review any open opportunities you own with a current close date in May/June and confirm the stage is correct (Prospecting / Discover / Eval / Negotiation / Commit).
- If a deal is no longer progressing, mark it Closed - Lost or Archive it with a 1-line reason.
- For any deal you expect to convert but that needs an internal approval (discount/extended term), add a 1-sentence note in the SF Opportunity "Commit rationale" field and flag me.

I've attached a quick export (stale-opps-export-20270420.csv) — it's the subset finance pulled that looks low-engagement. Focus on deals >60 days without activity.

Why this matters: the FP&A forecast is already using commit buckets; we need to minimize surprises for the board. If anything is ambiguous, call out the level of confidence: "P(Win)=70%" in the opportunity notes.

Thanks — short replies OK.

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Q2 accuracy sprint — stage locks & tidy-up (please action)

Stephanie — done a first pass. A few quick notes: 

- ACME (deal 00214-ACME) moved from Eval -> Negotiation, updated close to 2027-05-14, added "P(Win)=80%" to Commit rationale.
- BrightAI opportunity shows no activity since Jan; I left a "needs-qualification" note but haven't archived it yet because legal asked for an NDA last week.
- Uploaded a couple of rows with updated stage and short notes; see my comments column in the CSV.

If you want, I can ping ACME directly to confirm the calendar date — Marcus, you had the last call, want to confirm?

—Diego

Subject: Re: Q2 accuracy sprint — stage locks & tidy-up (please action)

Looping in Sienna for timeline clarity. Diego — thanks for the update on ACME. I can confirm we discussed the 05/14 date on our last call; counterparty legal was looking at contract language but there's no blocker on the budget side.

Sienna — can you confirm ACME's internal approval timing? If it's pushing, we'll either move the close date or change stage to Negotiation + Contingent.

Also attaching a quick MAP-checklist-template.docx (internal use) that I've been asking AEs to fill out for every "Commit" deal — one page, 3 bullets: procurement step, legal blocker, exec approval ETA. If you could have Marcus/Diego fill it and drop back in SF, finance will be happier.

—Marcus
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Thanks all — appreciated. Recap & next steps: 

- Diego: thanks for the CSV edits. Please finalize the ACME row with the MAP checklist and mark the opportunity "Commit" only once MAP is attached in SF.
- Marcus: please confirm ACME exec approval ETA in the SF notes (one-line).
- Neha: please run the attached stale-opps-export against your book and archive any deals that meet the archive criteria; add a 1-line reason in SF.
- Sienna / J. Reed (external) — if either of you sees any mismatch in dates/commit expectations, reply to this thread and we'll adjust the SF close date accordingly.

I'll pick up a final report Friday morning and send it to FP&A. If anything blocks you from the Thursday deadline, flag me and we'll triage.

—Stephanie

Redwood Inference
